title: Quick check: useState in Greater Depth

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the purpose of “useState in Greater Depth”?
options: The browser will infer all application behavior even if inputs and state are contradictory.
The concept allows application code to mutate React-managed DOM and state directly.
Lazy initialization should use state setters and immutable next values so React can update the UI predictably.
The concept removes the need to consider error states or accessibility.
questions.answer_key: Lazy initialization should use state setters and immutable next values so React can update the UI predictably.
questions.explanation: The correct choice is grounded in useState in Greater Depth: Lazy initialization should use state setters and immutable next values so React can update the UI predictably.

questions.prompt: Which practice is most reliable when applying Lazy initialization?
options: Optimize by adding every available Hook without measuring the result.
Use functional updates when the new value depends on previous state, and do not mutate objects or arrays.
Skip validation because a successful render proves that the application is correct.
Store duplicate copies of every value so each component can change it independently.
questions.answer_key: Use functional updates when the new value depends on previous state, and do not mutate objects or arrays.
questions.explanation: The correct choice is grounded in useState in Greater Depth: Use functional updates when the new value depends on previous state, and do not mutate objects or arrays.
